sourceFacts.fact: Hirschsprung disease has absent enteric nerve cells in a distal intestinal segment.
The affected segment cannot move stool normally, causing functional obstruction and neonatal symptoms.

labels: Hirschsprung disease: a failure of bowel propulsion
layout: Four large numbered tiles in a horizontal sequence. Tile1 uses three signal-dot positions with two as empty dashed circles; do not draw a neuron or nerve. Tile2 uses an interrupted abstract signal arrow ending at a stop mark. Tile3 uses neutral ochre square tokens backed up at an abstract stop line, not a bowel tube. Tile4 uses a clock and outward arrows as symptom tokens, no person or abdomen. Draw exactly three connectors between the four tiles. Under the row print: Functional blockage from missing nerve control.

requiredChecks: Four ordered concept nodes and three forward connections
No drawn nerve, ganglia, bowel or tissue layers
Abstract obstruction marker must not be described as a physical plug
No diagnostic time cutoff or claimed universal symptom
validation.pixelChecks: Pixel structure check: all four specified causal nodes with three forward connections. Missing-signal dots, failed arrow, stopped tokens and clock are explicitly abstract; token counts are not anatomical cell counts. Functional blockage from missing nerve control is labelled, with no nerve, tissue or bowel rendering. No time cutoff. Independent and clinical review pending.
